facts.text: In 1956, a dozen locals met at Leach Library and founded the Londonderry Historical Society to protect the town’s heritage.
The Society’s mission is to discover, procure, and preserve everything that relates to Londonderry’s natural, civil, literary, and ecclesiastical history.
Early members gathered artifacts, old documents, and began giving schoolchildren guided tours of historic sites across Londonderry.
From 1964 to 1977, Society members wrote and published five volumes titled Early Londonderry: Tidbits and Historical Sketches.
In 1977, the Society released History of Londonderry 1900‑1976 to celebrate the nation’s Bicentennial, funded by a $15,000 town grant.
The 1998 rescue of the Parmenter Barn and Clark Blacksmith Shop—relocated from High Range Road and Stonehenge Road—expanded the Society’s historic collection.
